general_world_news.title: 🌍 World News
general_world_news.content:
• **Russia/North Korea:** Russia deployed a North Korean ballistic missile in a strike on Ukraine on July 31, 2026, marking the first confirmed use of such weaponry in nearly a year. This indicates that Pyongyang has resupplied Moscow's depleted precision-strike inventories. The reappearance of these missiles deepens the sanctions-evading military partnership between Russia and North Korea. This development undercuts Western efforts to pressure Russia's missile supply and signals Moscow's sustained long-range strike capacity against Ukraine's rear.

• **China/Taiwan:** China has institutionalized a regularized Coast Guard presence east of Taiwan, moving beyond periodic incursions to establish a persistent presence ahead of a planned summit between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping. This strategic shift, noted on July 31, 2026, constitutes a quiet expansion of China's de facto jurisdictional claims in the region. This action creates new baseline facts on the ground that could potentially constrain future diplomatic negotiating room on Taiwan's status.

• **Spain/Italy/Morocco/EU:** On July 31, 2026, thousands of migrants stormed the border from Fnideq, Morocco, into the Spanish enclave of Ceuta, resulting in at least 57 confirmed deaths during the crossing attempts. The Spanish government responded by deploying its military to the area to restore order. In immediate consequence, Italy temporarily suspended the Schengen agreement with Spain on August 1, 2026, due to the border rush. This humanitarian crisis and Italy's Schengen suspension highlight growing pressures on European border management and internal freedom of movement, potentially straining EU unity and migration policies.

• **Iran/United States/Global Economy:** A brief lull in the military conflict between the US and Iran collapsed in late July 2026, as Iran launched renewed drone and missile attacks on US bases in Jordan, prompting the US to resume military action. Despite US President Donald Trump's claims of diplomatic progress, active exchanges of strikes continue, causing Brent crude prices to rebound 7.5% to $88.13 per barrel and West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude to rise 6.3% to $85.53 per barrel on July 31, 2026. The renewed hostilities and consistently high energy prices, which remain 30-40% above pre-war levels, are projected to slow global real GDP growth to 3.0% in 2026 and sustain elevated inflation, impacting global economic stability and supply chains.

Why it matters: Today's top stories indicate a volatile global landscape marked by escalating geopolitical tensions, the resurgence of military partnerships impacting ongoing conflicts, a humanitarian crisis challenging European cooperation, and renewed regional conflicts pushing energy prices higher, collectively signaling increased risks to global economic stability and international relations.

eu_policy.title: 🇪🇺 European Union Policy
eu_policy.content:
• **EU Digital Omnibus on Artificial Intelligence (Regulation (EU) 2026/1744):** This Regulation, which entered into force on July 27, 2026, amends the Artificial Intelligence Act (AI Act) to streamline implementation and reduce compliance burdens. Previously, obligations for standalone high-risk AI systems (Annex III) were set to apply earlier; now, they will apply from December 2, 2027. Similarly, rules for high-risk AI embedded in physical products (Annex I) previously had an earlier application, but now apply from August 2, 2028. Additionally, simplified documentation measures, previously only for SMEs, are now extended to medium-sized companies, and previous AI literacy requirements for companies are simplified, with the Commission and Member States taking a stronger role. The Regulation also introduces a prohibition on AI systems that generate non-consensual sexually explicit or child sexual abuse material ("nudification apps"). This provides businesses with extended timelines for complying with significant high-risk AI system requirements and reduces administrative burdens for a wider range of companies, but introduces new prohibitions on harmful AI applications.

• **AI Act Transparency Obligations (Article 50 of the AI Act):** These transparency rules will enter into force on August 2, 2026, imposing new requirements on providers and deployers of certain AI systems. Previously, there were no specific EU-wide legal requirements for labeling AI-generated content. Now, providers of generative and interactive AI systems must inform users whenever they are directly interacting with an AI. For synthetic content like deepfakes (AI-generated or manipulated images, audio, or video), providers must apply machine-readable marks to ensure the content is identifiable as artificially generated. Deployers of AI systems must also inform individuals when they are exposed to emotion recognition, biometric categorization tools, deepfakes, or AI-generated text publications on public interest issues without human review. Providers of General-Purpose AI (GPAI) models will also face new obligations regarding risk management, copyright policies, and publishing summaries of training content. This significantly increases transparency and accountability for AI developers and users, aiming to build public trust and prevent misinformation and manipulation.

• **EU Right to Repair Directive:** This Directive entered into force on July 31, 2026, aiming to promote sustainable consumption by making product repair more accessible and attractive across the EU. Previously, consumers often faced difficulties and high costs when trying to repair faulty products outside the legal guarantee period, often leading to premature disposal. Now, consumers have the right to request manufacturers to repair products such as smartphones, washing machines, and fridges, even after the legal guarantee has expired. Manufacturers are obliged to offer these repairs at a reasonable price and within a reasonable timeframe, provide clear information on their repair services and indicative prices on their websites, and ensure spare parts are accessible and affordable. Furthermore, manufacturers are prohibited from employing contractual clauses, hardware, or software techniques that impede repairs. When a product is repaired within its liability period, its legal guarantee will be extended by at least 12 months. This shifts the burden towards manufacturers to support product longevity, reduces waste, and offers consumers more sustainable and potentially cost-effective options for their goods.

Why it matters: This week marks a significant step in the EU's push for a more transparent and sustainable digital and consumer economy, with new rules on AI transparency and consumer repair rights taking effect, alongside the refinement of existing AI regulations.

ai_productivity.title: ⚡ AI & Productivity
ai_productivity.content:
• **OpenAI GPT-5.6 (Luna, Terra, Sol):** OpenAI has implemented significant price reductions for its GPT-5.6 Luna (80% less) and Terra (20% less) models, alongside introducing a faster "Fast mode" option for GPT-5.6 Sol in the API. Luna is now priced at $0.20 per million input tokens and $1.20 per million output tokens, while Terra costs $2 per million input and $12 per million output, aimed at improving price-performance across enterprise workloads, with Luna specifically enhanced for cost-effective, high-volume agentic tasks. Developers and knowledge workers can now execute complex, high-volume agentic workflows with GPT-5.6 Luna at dramatically lower costs, making it economically viable to automate extensive data processing or large-scale content generation.

• **DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731:** DeepSeek has officially released the DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 API in public beta, a 284B total / 13B active parameter Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model featuring a 1 million token context window. This version, retaining its original architecture, boasts significantly enhanced autonomous agent capabilities and reduced API costs (e.g., $0.14/1M input cache-miss, $0.28/1M output), now natively supporting OpenAI's Responses API format adapted for Codex in addition to its existing Anthropic compatibility. Developers can leverage this more capable and cost-efficient model for building sophisticated agentic applications, such as autonomously generating and debugging multi-step code, reducing reliance on more expensive alternatives.

• **Perplexity Projects on Computer:** Perplexity launched "Projects" on its Computer agent, transforming it into a "multiplayer agentic operating system for work." This update enables persistent memory, files, and sessions to be scoped across multiple users and hubs, offers a shared file system for collaborators, integrates with Google Workspace and Slack, and extends Computer Brain's self-improvement capabilities to learn from collective team activity. Teams can now centralize and collaborate on complex, multi-step AI-driven projects directly within Perplexity Computer, allowing the AI to learn from shared tasks and autonomously manage a cross-functional initiative like drafting, researching, and organizing a new product launch plan.

• **Google DeepMind Gemini Robotics ER 2 and ER 2 Streaming (public preview):** Google DeepMind released Gemini Robotics ER 2 and ER 2 Streaming, embodied reasoning models in public preview for robotics. These models provide advanced spatial reasoning, agentic code execution, multi-step tool orchestration, video analysis, and multi-robot coordination, with ER 2 Streaming optimized for real-time, low-latency robot agents using bidirectional audio and video input, extending control from tabletop manipulation to full-body humanoid robots. Robotics developers can now build and deploy more sophisticated, real-time multi-robot systems capable of complex physical tasks and human-like interaction, enabling a robot team to autonomously manage a multi-stage assembly line with fluid transitions and error recovery.

Why it matters: The AI landscape is rapidly shifting towards more capable and affordable agentic systems, both in general-purpose models and specialized productivity tools, facilitating a new era of automated collaboration and physical AI interaction.

portugal_policy.title: 🇵🇹 Portugal Policy & Law
portugal_policy.content:
•   **Novas Regras para o Crédito à Habitação:** As novas recomendações macroprudenciais do Banco de Portugal entraram em vigor a 1 de agosto de 2026, estabelecendo critérios mais rigorosos para a concessão de crédito. Anteriormente, a taxa de esforço máxima recomendada para a totalidade dos empréstimos era de 50% do rendimento líquido mensal; agora, este limite foi reduzido para 45%. Além disso, os prazos máximos de maturidade dos empréstimos foram ajustados, com o limite de 40 anos para mutuários até 35 anos e 35 anos para mutuários com mais de 35 anos, simplificando os escalões anteriores. Os bancos também deixam de poder financiar 100% do valor de imóveis que lhes pertencem. O impacto prático é um acesso mais restrito e cauteloso ao crédito para a aquisição de casa e outros bens de consumo para os cidadãos.

•   **Revisão das Taxas do Imposto sobre Produtos Petrolíferos e Energéticos (ISP):** A Portaria n.º 320-D/2026/1, publicada a 31 de julho e com entrada em vigor a 3 de agosto de 2026, procede à revisão e fixação das taxas unitárias do ISP aplicáveis à gasolina sem chumbo e ao gasóleo rodoviário no continente. Em comparação com as taxas em vigor (anteriormente da Portaria n.º 314-B/2026/1), as novas taxas passam a ser de 445,10 € por 1000 litros para gasolina sem chumbo (já com a consignação de serviço rodoviário de 87 €) e 282,84 € por 1000 litros para gasóleo rodoviário (já com a consignação de serviço rodoviário de 111 €). O impacto prático é uma alteração direta nos preços dos combustíveis na bomba para consumidores e empresas a partir de segunda-feira.

•   **Adiamento da Entrada em Vigor do Novo Regime Jurídico da Urbanização e Edificação (RJUE):** O Decreto-Lei n.º 155-B/2026, publicado a 31 de julho, prorroga a entrada em vigor do Decreto-Lei n.º 108/2026, de 29 de maio, que revista profundamente o Regime Jurídico da Urbanização e Edificação (RJUE). A data de entrada em vigor, inicialmente prevista para 3 de agosto de 2026, foi adiada para 1 de outubro de 2026. Esta decisão visa dar mais tempo aos municípios para adaptarem as suas plataformas informáticas e implementarem a regulamentação complementar. O impacto prático é a manutenção do regime anterior de licenciamento urbanístico por mais dois meses, permitindo que promotores imobiliários, arquitetos e donos de obra se preparem para as significativas mudanças nas regras de construção e reabilitação.

•   **Autorização para a Criação da Prestação Social Única (PSU):** A Lei n.º 36/2026, de 27 de julho, publicada a 28 de julho, autoriza o Governo a instituir a Prestação Social Única. Este novo modelo de apoio social tem como objetivo agregar 13 prestações sociais existentes, incluindo vários apoios a pessoas e famílias com menos recursos, para simplificar e harmonizar as regras de acesso e reduzir procedimentos administrativos. Anteriormente, as famílias tinham de gerir múltiplos regimes de apoio; agora, a lei estabelece a base para a sua consolidação numa única prestação, cujo valor variará consoante a dimensão e rendimentos do agregado familiar. O impacto prático será a simplificação do acesso aos apoios sociais para as famílias mais vulneráveis, uma vez que o Governo aprovará nos próximos dias o decreto-lei que define as condições de acesso e o regime jurídico da nova prestação.

•   **Prorrogação de Prazos para Regulamentação Municipal do Alojamento Local:** O Decreto-Lei n.º 151/2026, publicado a 30 de julho, prorroga até 31 de dezembro de 2026 o prazo para os municípios com mais de mil unidades de alojamento local (registadas até 31 de dezembro de 2025) decidirem sobre a elaboração ou alteração dos seus regulamentos. Este diploma também permite que os municípios prolonguem suspensões existentes ou imponham novas suspensões de novos registos, limitadas ao período estritamente necessário para a conclusão da regulamentação e sem exceder o final de 2026. O impacto prático é a extensão da capacidade regulatória dos municípios sobre o Alojamento Local, proporcionando um período adicional de moratória e flexibilidade para a legislação local, o que afeta a abertura de novos estabelecimentos e a segurança jurídica dos operadores.

Why it matters: As novas regras do Banco de Portugal tornam o acesso ao crédito à habitação mais rigoroso, enquanto as alterações fiscais nos combustíveis e os adiamentos em regulamentações-chave como o RJUE e o Alojamento Local têm um impacto direto no custo de vida, na construção e na atividade económica, com a criação da Prestação Social Única a sinalizar uma futura simplificação nos apoios sociais.

us_policy.title: 🇺🇸 United States Policy
us_policy.content:
• **Presidential Determination on Recoverable Critical Minerals and Materials (CMMs):** On July 30, 2026, President Donald J. Trump signed a Presidential Determination under Section 101 of the Defense Production Act of 1950. This action delegates immediate authority to the Secretary of Commerce to institute export restrictions on recoverable critical minerals and materials (CMMs), which are deemed essential for national defense and whose foreign reliance threatens supply chain disruptions. Previously, such explicit authority for the Commerce Secretary to restrict CMM exports under the DPA was not in place; now, the Secretary possesses this power immediately. This significantly enhances the U.S. government's capacity to secure domestic supplies of vital materials, potentially influencing global commodity markets and the supply chains of industries dependent on these minerals.

• **Treasury Sanctions on Iran-Related Networks:** On July 29 and July 30, 2026, the U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) issued new sanctions under Executive Order 13224. On July 29, OFAC targeted the Persian Gulf Marine Insurance Company and HormuzSafe Marine Services Authority for their role in Iran's maritime "extortion operation" in the Strait of Hormuz. On July 30, OFAC sanctioned six entities and individuals across China, Russia, Iran, and India for supporting Mahan Air, an Iranian airline affiliated with the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC)-Quds Force, which facilitates personnel travel and drone component transport. These actions immediately block all property and interests in property subject to U.S. jurisdiction of the designated persons, prohibiting transactions with them by U.S. persons. This intensifies financial pressure on Iran's destabilizing activities and associated support networks, potentially affecting international shipping and aviation sectors with ties to the region.

• **DHS Expands Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act (UFLPA) Entity List:** On July 31, 2026, the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) announced the addition of 43 Chinese companies to the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act (UFLPA) Entity List, in what was termed the list's largest-ever expansion. These new designations, effective Monday, August 3, 2026, target entities primarily involved in metals and mining. Previously, goods from these companies could potentially enter the U.S.; now, imports from these 43 companies are presumed to be made with forced labor and are prohibited from entering the U.S. unless importers can provide clear and convincing evidence to the contrary. This action reinforces the U.S. commitment to combating forced labor and will necessitate increased supply chain scrutiny and potential diversification away from Chinese suppliers for affected industries.

• **CFTC Fines George Santos for Manipulative Trading:** On July 31, 2026, the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) ordered former Republican Representative George Santos to pay $35,000 for alleged manipulative trading. Santos was found to have made false statements on social media that benefited his wagers on prediction market event contracts on the platform Kalshi, subsequently earning nearly $18,000 by not attending President Trump's State of the Union address. The order mandates he repay the approximately $18,000 earned, with the remainder as a civil monetary penalty. This enforcement action highlights the CFTC's active oversight of prediction markets and manipulative trading practices, establishing a precedent for individual accountability in these nascent financial instruments.

• **Presidential Proclamation on Quartz Surface Products:** On July 31, 2026, President Donald J. Trump issued a Presidential Proclamation "To Facilitate Positive Adjustment to Competition from Imports of Quartz Surface Products." This proclamation indicates a new trade action designed to address competition from imported quartz surface products, likely involving modifications to existing trade measures or the imposition of new tariffs or quotas to protect domestic industries. This signifies the administration's ongoing use of trade tools to safeguard specific U.S. industries.

Why it matters: The U.S. government has significantly escalated its economic and trade policy actions this week, focusing on securing critical supply chains, intensifying sanctions against foreign adversaries, and enhancing regulatory enforcement in emerging markets.
